formTitle: Request for Reconsideration on the Updating and Extension of Authorized Stay
checkoutEligibleNote: Not yet decided -- same open business-classification question as the other mapped forms. This mapping covers field-level automation only; checkout eligibility is a separate business decision.
reproductionRightsNote: Confirmed directly on the form itself: 'This document may be reproduced and is NOT FOR SALE'. Also independently confirmed by the existing R2 inventory (bi-forms-library/inventory/forms-library-inventory.json): reproduction="may_be_reproduced".
derivedFrom: Measured programmatically from a 300 DPI raster of the real original PDF (downloaded from the private fis-bi-forms-library R2 bucket, originals/2014-01-011.pdf). Unlike every comb-box-style form mapped so far, this is a narrative/affidavit letter-format document with inline underscore blanks embedded in running paragraph text, not a grid of per-character cells -- confirmed by reading pdftotext -layout's complete output before attempting any measurement. Every blank's x-range was found by a full-page scan for near-black (ink, not grey comb-box-border) horizontal pixel runs longer than 20px, clustered into rows, then matched to its surrounding sentence by cross-referencing the same row's position against pdftotext -layout's reading order -- not assumed from guesswork. A pixel-ruled visual crop of the two multi-line 'reason' paragraphs was used to directly confirm which blank-line cluster belongs to which paragraph and in which order, since several inline trigger-blanks (e.g. 'for the reason that ____' at the end of a wrapped line) could otherwise be confused with the unrelated 'with contact number(s) ____' blank directly above it -- an initial raw reading of the row list did exactly that (misread the contact-number blank's row as belonging to the reason paragraph) before the visual crop resolved it.

measurementNotes.entirelyCustomerSupplied: Like 2021-03-001 (Travel Pass) and unlike the comb-box forms, this form's complete text was read start to finish and contains no BI-staff-only data-entry section -- it is a sworn, self-written letter ending in the applicant's own (and, conditionally, a representative's) signature. customerPreviewCropBox therefore covers the full page.
measurementNotes.inlineBlankMisattributionCaught: See derivedFrom above for the contact-number/reason-paragraph row confusion caught and corrected by direct visual inspection before any coordinate was finalized.
measurementNotes.civilStatusCheckboxes: These are small inline-text checkbox glyphs (part of the paragraph's own font, roughly 6x6pt) rather than large drawn boxes like 2021-03-001's Section I checkboxes -- directly measured via the same near-black pixel-run scan (their glyph ink registers the same way an underscore run does), not estimated from label proportions.
measurementNotes.conditionalRepresentativeSection: representativeAccreditationNo and representativeRelationship (and the representative's own unpopulated wet-ink signature line) are only relevant if the application is filed by an authorized representative rather than the applicant in person -- included as ordinary optional customer-supplied fields, same treatment as 2021-03-001's conditional spouse fields.
measurementNotes.fiveLineReasonFieldsDesignNote: This form's two multi-line narrative answers (reason failed to extend / reason wanting to stay longer) are exposed in questionnaire.json as 5 separate line-by-line questions each, rather than one free-text textarea auto-wrapped across lines -- the shared engine's wrappedPairs binding only supports exactly 2 lines (see bi-forms-library/engine/lib/field-bindings.js), and extending it to N lines was judged out of scope for a single form's mapping. Each line is a plain direct 1:1 field (no binding needed) so the customer (or assisting staff) composes their statement across up to 5 short lines instead of one paragraph.
measurementNotes.nationalityFieldCorrection: A first automated pass placed nationality's blank at pdf_y 683.76 (x 72-494.88), derived from a misread row in the initial full-page underline scan. The first generated test PDF showed the sample nationality text rendering directly on top of the 'single/married/...' civil-status checkbox row, overlapping its glyphs. Direct pixel inspection of the real original (cross-checked against pdftotext -bbox, which shows exactly one underscore token in this area: xMin 72.024-210.875, yMin 258.51 top-space) found the real, and only, blank immediately below the checkboxes at pdf_y 668.76 (x 72-210.72) -- captioned '(Civil Status)' directly beneath it, with a second caption '(Nationality)' positioned further right (x 474-527) but with NO corresponding blank of its own anywhere on the page at any darkness threshold tested. Concluded this single blank serves double duty as the write-in answer following the Civil Status checkboxes AND the 'a citizen of ___' nationality prompt (the two captions apply to the same blank, however the original form's own layout intends it) -- there is nowhere else on the form a nationality answer could go. Corrected and confirmed clear of the checkbox row in a regenerated test PDF.

If a representative is filing on your behalf, they must also sign and attach a photocopy of valid government-issued identification and a Special Power of Attorney (SPA).
